biography.plain_text: Ettore Lonati is an Italian industrialist and honorary president of Lonati S.p.A., the textile-machinery company founded by his father, Francesco. He led the Brescia group through expansion into steel, electronics, property and food before transferring operations to a third generation in 2024. He also chairs Alfa Acciai and two technical-education foundations.

long_biography.plain_text:
Technical education became the bridge between Ettore Lonati's industrial career and his civic work in Brescia. The foundation carrying his parents' names supports advanced textile training, scientific study, culture, health and social assistance. Its work translates the family's manufacturing experience into programmes for younger people and community institutions.

Lonati also helped create the city's Anglo-American school and remains president of ITS Academy Machina Lonati, which links post-secondary study to design, fashion, technology and business. A partnership with Brescia's chamber of commerce continues this technical-education work through a planned training campus. These education roles endured after he stepped back from operating Lonati S.p.A.

uncertainties: Ettore Lonati is distinguished from founder Francesco; brothers Fausto and Tiberio; and later-generation Marco, Riccardo, Francesco and Adele through exact birth, father-son, company, chair and succession evidence. No role belonging to another Lonati is assigned to Ettore.

Inherited and expanded reflects succession to the father-founded industrial platform plus Ettore's documented operating expansion into steel and other sectors. The reviewed sources do not disclose his exact inherited share, current percentage or division among siblings and descendants, so no ownership percentage is inferred.

Operator describes decades of material leadership and expansion rather than a claim that Ettore remains Lonati S.p.A.'s day-to-day executive. He moved to honorary president in 2024, while Marco, Riccardo and Francesco assumed operating authority; his current Alfa Acciai and education-chair roles remain separately documented.

Manufacturing captures the textile-machinery platform that originally created the family fortune. Diversified captures the current group across textile machinery, steel, electronics, property, food, education and services; it does not imply that every company or sector is personally owned by Ettore in an unstated proportion.

The immutable complete birth date is corroborated by CONSOB, which also supplies Botticino, Brescia as the birthplace. Botticino Sera appears in secondary biographies, but the official regulator uses Botticino, so the broader municipality form is proposed.

The Lonati Foundation's public pages and separate institutional agreements show changing board descriptions over time. The biography uses the durable foundation mission and current signed or directly published chair roles rather than assuming that every historical title remains unchanged.

Group revenues, production shares, transaction totals, steel output, real-estate values and media net-worth estimates describe companies or fluctuate over time, so none is used as a personal wealth figure or durable biography claim.

Current and historical vessel facts, politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sensitive private-family details and transient financial metrics were excluded from both biographies and classification narrative.
